blurb.en: Choose the right word in a short story and fill the gaps in a letter from a word box.
blurb.vi: Chọn đúng từ trong một câu chuyện ngắn và điền vào chỗ trống trong lá thư bằng các từ trong hộp từ.

past simple.def: The verb form for finished actions, like 'went', 'played' and 'was'.
past simple.ex: 'We played football yesterday' is in the *past simple*.

present continuous.def: am, is or are + a verb with -ing, like 'is reading' or 'are visiting'.
present continuous.ex: 'She is reading now' is in the *present continuous*.

plan.def: Something you have decided to do later, often on a day or at a time.
plan.ex: Our *plan* is to visit the zoo on Saturday.

time clue.def: Words like yesterday, now or next week that tell you which verb form to use.
time clue.ex: 'Last night' is a *time clue*: it tells you to use the past simple.

preposition.def: A small word like at, in, of or about. It often comes after an adjective.

quantifier.def: A word that tells you how many or how much, like both, all, fewer or less.
quantifier.ex: 'Fewer' is a *quantifier* for things we can count.

relative word.def: Who, which or where: it adds information about a person, a thing or a place.
relative word.ex: In 'the man who sings', 'who' is a *relative word*.

indefinite pronoun.def: A word like someone, anything, everyone or nobody, when we don't say exactly who or what.

comparative.def: An adjective form like bigger or more beautiful. We use it with 'than'.

word box.def: A list printed above a text. You choose from it to fill the gaps.
word box.ex: Choose each answer from the *word box*.

gap.def: An empty space in a sentence where something is missing.

extra.def: More than you need. Some words in the box are not used.
extra.ex: There are two *extra* words in the box, so you won't use them all.

countable.def: Nouns like apples, chairs or friends. You can say one, two, three of them.

uncountable.def: Nouns like water, rice or sugar. You can't say one, two, three of them.

title.vi: Hôm qua, bây giờ và tuần sau

scenes.head: Finn's diary
scenes.html: *Yesterday* *was* my cousin's birthday. There *were* twenty people at his house, and we *played* games in the garden. There *was* a big chocolate cake too. Right *now* I *am writing* my diary in bed. *Next Saturday* my cousin and I *are visiting* the zoo together. I can't wait!

steps.en: *was*, *were* and *played* are past simple. The time clue is *Yesterday*.
steps.vi: *was*, *were* và *played* là thì quá khứ đơn. Từ chỉ thời gian là *Yesterday*.

steps.en: Use *there was* for one thing and *there were* for many things.
steps.vi: Dùng *there was* cho một vật và *there were* cho nhiều vật.

steps.en: *am writing* is happening *now*. *are visiting* is a plan: look for *Next Saturday*.
steps.vi: *am writing* đang xảy ra *now* (bây giờ). *are visiting* là một kế hoạch: hãy tìm *Next Saturday*.

title.vi: Từ nhỏ đi sau tính từ

scenes.head: Ana's message to her friend
scenes.html: I'm *good at* swimming, but I'm *afraid of* deep water. My coach is very *kind to* me and never shouts. *Both* my brothers are in the club too. Before a race, we eat *fewer* sweets and drink *less* juice. My mum is always *proud of* us!

steps.en: Some adjectives always take the same small word: *good at*, *afraid of*, *kind to*, *proud of*, *interested in*, *worried about*.
steps.vi: Một số tính từ luôn đi với cùng một từ nhỏ: *good at*, *afraid of*, *kind to*, *proud of*, *interested in*, *worried about*.

steps.en: *fewer* is for things you can count (sweets). *less* is for things you can't count (juice).
steps.vi: *fewer* dùng cho thứ đếm được (sweets). *less* dùng cho thứ không đếm được (juice).

steps.en: *Both* is for two people or things. *All* is for three or more.
steps.vi: *Both* dùng cho hai người hoặc hai vật. *All* dùng cho ba hoặc nhiều hơn.

scenes.head: Part of a letter with a word box
scenes.html:
Word box: nothing, someone, where, which, who

Yesterday I went to the market *where* my grandma buys fruit. I met a woman *who* sells mangoes. She gave me a mango *which* was very sweet. *Someone* was playing music, but there was *nothing* to sit on, so we stood and listened.

steps.en: *who* is for people, *which* is for things and *where* is for places.
steps.vi: *who* dùng cho người, *which* dùng cho vật và *where* dùng cho nơi chốn.

steps.en: *someone* and *something* go in positive sentences. *anyone* and *anything* go in questions and after 'not'. *nobody* and *nothing* mean 'not one'.
steps.vi: *someone* và *something* dùng trong câu khẳng định. *anyone* và *anything* dùng trong câu hỏi và sau 'not'. *nobody* và *nothing* nghĩa là 'không ai / không gì'.

steps.en: With a word box, try each word in the gap and read the whole sentence. Use each word only once.
steps.vi: Với hộp từ, hãy thử từng từ vào chỗ trống và đọc cả câu. Mỗi từ chỉ dùng một lần.

end.en: Brilliant! You chose the right verb forms and small grammar words.
end.vi: Tuyệt vời! Em đã chọn đúng dạng động từ và các từ ngữ pháp nhỏ.

challenge.result: You spotted verb forms, prepositions, quantifiers and who / which / where!

v.q: Which sentence is about a plan for the future?
opts: We are flying to Hue on Friday.
We flew to Hue with Grandma last Friday.
We fly to Hue every summer.
whys: 'last Friday' is in the past, so this is not a plan.
'every summer' is something we do again and again, not one plan.
v.hint: Look for am / is / are + -ing and a future time.
v.worked: *are flying* + *on Friday* (a future day) = a plan.

v.q: Last year there ________ a big mango tree in our garden.
whys: 'were' is for many things, but there is only one tree.
'Last year' is in the past, so 'is' is wrong.
v.hint: Is it one tree or many? Is it now or in the past?
v.worked: One tree, *Last year*: there *was* a big mango tree.

v.q: Phuc is very interested ________ old cars and trains.
whys: We say 'good at', but not 'interested at'.
We say 'afraid of', but not 'interested of'.
v.hint: Which small word always goes with 'interested'?
v.worked: We always say *interested in*.

v.q: Which words are correct?
whys: 'proud at' is not English. Think of 'afraid ...' and 'proud ...'.
'proud in' is not English. Which small word goes with 'proud'?
v.hint: Say each one quietly. Which small word goes with 'proud'?
v.worked: We always say *proud of*: I'm *proud of* my team.

v.q: There are ________ children in my class than in your class.
whys: 'less' is for things we can't count, like water. We can count children.
'much' is for things we can't count, like rice. We can count children.
v.hint: Can you count children? Look at the noun after the gap.
v.worked: *children* can be counted, so we use *fewer*.

v.q: Please put ________ sugar in my tea. It's too sweet!
whys: 'fewer' is for things we can count. We can't count sugar.
'many' is for things we can count, like sweets, not sugar.
v.hint: Can you count sugar? Read why the tea is a problem.
v.worked: *sugar* can't be counted, and the tea is too sweet: *less* sugar.

v.q: This is the shop ________ we buy our bread every morning.
whys: 'who' is for people, but a shop is a place.
'which' is for things. Here the shop is the place we go to.
v.hint: Is the word before the gap a person, a thing or a place?
v.worked: A shop is a place where something happens: *where*.

v.q: I knocked on the door, but ________ answered. The house was empty.
whys: If the house was empty, there was no person to answer.
'anybody' needs 'not' before it, like 'didn't answer'.
v.hint: Read the last sentence. Was there a person inside?
v.worked: The house was *empty*, so *nobody* answered.

blurb.en: Practise one grammar point at a time, then type the missing word.
blurb.vi: Luyện từng điểm ngữ pháp, rồi gõ từ còn thiếu.

v.q: Yesterday, my grandpa ________ us a funny story about his school days.
whys: 'tells' is for every day, but 'Yesterday' is in the past.
'telling' needs 'was' before it. Here the story is a finished action.
v.hint: Find the time word at the start of the sentence.
v.worked: *Yesterday* is in the past, so we use the past simple: *told*.

v.q: Two years ago, there ________ only one small shop in our street.
whys: 'is' is for now, but 'Two years ago' is in the past.
'are' is for now and for many things. Here there is one shop, in the past.
v.hint: Find the time words. Is it one shop or many?
v.worked: *Two years ago* + one shop: there *was*.

v.q: We ________ our cousins in Da Lat next weekend. The tickets are booked!
whys: 'visited' is past, but 'next weekend' is in the future.
'were visiting' is past, but 'next weekend' is in the future.
v.hint: Find the time words. Is this a plan for the future?
v.worked: *next weekend* + tickets booked = a plan: we *are visiting*.

v.q: Look! Ivy ________ a poster about healthy food for our classroom.
whys: 'makes' is for every day. 'Look!' tells you it is happening now.
'made' is finished. 'Look!' tells you it is happening now.
v.hint: What does 'Look!' tell you about the time?
v.worked: *Look!* = it is happening now, so we use *is making*.

v.q: The film about the lost city was so ________ that I watched it twice.
whys: 'excited' is how a person feels. A film doesn't have feelings.
'excite' is a verb, so it can't come after 'was so'.
v.hint: Is the word about the film, or about how a person feels?
v.worked: The film makes you feel something, so we use the -ing word: *exciting*.

v.q: I felt ________ because there was nothing to do on the rainy afternoon.
whys: 'boring' describes the thing, like a boring film. Here it is how I felt.
'bore' is a verb, so it can't come after 'I felt'.
v.hint: Look at 'I felt'. Is the word about a person's feeling?
v.worked: *I felt* is about my feeling, so we use the -ed word: *bored*.

title.vi: Giới từ, từ chỉ số lượng và someone

v.q: My sister is very good ________ drawing animals.
whys: We say 'interested in', but not 'good in'.
We say 'afraid of', but not 'good of'.
v.hint: Which small word always goes with 'good'?
v.worked: We always say *good at*: good *at* drawing.

v.q: Are you afraid ________ spiders and snakes?
whys: We say 'good at', but not 'afraid at'.
We say 'worried about', but not 'afraid about'.
v.hint: Which small word always goes with 'afraid'?
v.worked: We always say *afraid of*.

v.q: I drink ________ water than my brother, so I am often thirsty.
whys: 'fewer' is for things we can count. We can't count water.
'many' is for things we can count, like bottles, not water.
v.hint: Can you count water? Then read why I am thirsty.
v.worked: *water* can't be counted, so we use *less*: less water, so I'm thirsty.

v.q: ________ my parents can speak English and French.
whys: 'All' is for three or more. You have two parents.
'Much' is for things we can't count, like rice, not people.
v.hint: How many parents do you have?
v.worked: Two parents, so we use *Both*.

v.q: I'm hungry, but there isn't ________ in the fridge.
whys: 'isn't' already says 'not', so 'nothing' makes two 'not' words.
After 'not' we don't use 'something'.
v.hint: Find 'isn't'. Which word goes after 'not'?
v.worked: After *isn't* we use *anything*: there isn't anything.

v.q: I heard a knock at the door. ________ is outside!
whys: 'Anyone' is for questions and sentences with 'not'.
Somebody knocked, so it can't be that no person is outside.
v.hint: Read the first sentence. Who knocked?
v.worked: A person knocked, and the sentence is positive: *Someone* is outside.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: This is the café {0} we have noodles every Sunday.
v.hint: The café is a place. Which relative word is for places?
v.worked: For a place we use *where*: the café *where* we have noodles.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: I have a friend {0} can speak three languages.
v.hint: A friend is a person. Which relative word is for people?
v.worked: For a person we use *who*: a friend *who* can speak three languages.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: Last night there {0} lots of fireworks in the sky.
v.hint: 'Last night' is past. Is it one firework or many?
v.worked: Past + many fireworks: there *were*.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: Yesterday there {0} a big storm, so we stayed inside.
v.hint: 'Yesterday' is past. Is it one storm or many?
v.worked: Past + one storm: there *was*.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: A giraffe is taller {0} an elephant.
v.hint: 'taller' compares two animals. Which word comes after it?
v.worked: After a comparative we use *than*: taller *than*.

v.q: Write ONE word in the gap.
lines: This mango is sweeter {0} the one we bought yesterday.
v.hint: 'sweeter' compares two mangoes. Which word comes after it?
v.worked: After a comparative we use *than*: sweeter *than*.

title.vi: Phần 1: một câu chuyện, năm câu

v.q:
Story: Hamid and the mosquitoes (sentence 1 of 5)
Last summer, Hamid ________ a week at his grandparents' house in the countryside.
whys: 'Last summer' is finished time, so the base form is wrong.
'spending' needs 'was' before it, and this is a finished action.
v.hint: Find the time words at the start of the sentence.
v.worked: *Last summer* is finished time, so we use the past simple: Hamid *spent* a week there.

v.q:
Story: The hole in the pavement (sentence 1 of 5)
Last Sunday, Bella ________ to see a giant chalk picture on the pavement outside the library.
whys: 'Last Sunday' is finished time, so the base form is wrong.
'going' needs 'was' before it, and this is a finished action.
v.hint: Find the time words at the start of the sentence.
v.worked: *Last Sunday* is finished time, so we use the past simple: Bella *went*.

v.q:
Story: Hamid and the mosquitoes (sentence 2 of 5)
On the first evening, mosquitoes bit his legs, and the itchy bites were really ________.
whys: 'annoyed' is how a person feels. Bites don't have feelings.
'annoy' is a verb, so it can't come after 'were really'.
v.hint: Is the word about a person's feeling, or about the thing that causes the feeling?
v.worked: The bites cause the feeling, so we use the -ing word: the bites were *annoying*.

v.q:
Story: The hole in the pavement (sentence 2 of 5)
The picture looked like a deep hole in the ground, and it was really ________.
whys: 'amazed' is how a person feels. A picture doesn't have feelings.
'amaze' is a verb, so it can't come after 'was really'.
v.hint: Is the word about a person's feeling, or about the thing that causes the feeling?
v.worked: The picture causes the feeling, so we use the -ing word: it was *amazing*.

v.q:
Story: Hamid and the mosquitoes (sentence 3 of 5)
That night, Grandma gave him ________ to stop the bites: a big white net for his bed.
whys: We use 'anything' in questions and after 'not'. This sentence is positive.
Read after the colon (:). Grandma gave him a net, so 'nothing' is wrong.
v.hint: Read the part after the colon (:). Did Grandma give him a thing?
v.worked: She gave him a net, in a positive sentence: Grandma gave him *something*.

v.q:
Story: The hole in the pavement (sentence 3 of 5)
At first, Bella was afraid to stand on it, but ________ else was jumping over the 'hole' and laughing.
whys: We use 'anyone' in questions and after 'not'. This sentence is positive.
'but' shows the other people were different from Bella, and they were laughing.
v.hint: 'but' tells you the other people did something different. What were they doing?
v.worked: Bella was afraid, *but* the other people were jumping and laughing: *everyone* else.

v.q:
Story: Hamid and the mosquitoes (sentence 4 of 5)
It was the same net ________ Hamid's mum used when she was a little girl!
whys: 'who' is for people, but a net is a thing.
'where' is for places, but a net is a thing.
v.hint: Look at the word before the gap. Is it a person, a thing or a place?
v.worked: A net is a thing, so we use *which*: the net *which* his mum used.

v.q:
Story: The hole in the pavement (sentence 4 of 5)
Then she met the young woman ________ made the picture in only two days.
whys: 'which' is for things, but a young woman is a person.
'where' is for places, but a young woman is a person.
v.hint: Look at the words before the gap. Is it a person, a thing or a place?
v.worked: A young woman is a person, so we use *who*: the woman *who* made it.

v.q:
Story: Hamid and the mosquitoes (sentence 5 of 5)
Hamid loved his stay, and he ________ his grandparents again next month.
whys: 'visited' is past, but 'next month' is in the future.
'he visit' is not correct English. Look for a plan with a future time.
v.hint: Find the time words at the end. Is this a plan?
v.worked: *next month* shows a plan, so we use the present continuous: he *is visiting*.

v.q:
Story: The hole in the pavement (sentence 5 of 5)
Bella loved it, and next weekend she ________ her own pavement picture at home.
whys: 'drew' is past, but 'next weekend' is in the future.
'was drawing' is past, but 'next weekend' is in the future.
v.hint: Find the time words. Is this a plan?
v.worked: *next weekend* shows a plan, so we use the present continuous: she *is drawing*.

v.q: Read the letter. Write ONE word from the box for gap 18.
lines: It is much bigger {0} our old one.
v.hint: Find 'bigger'. Which box word comes after a comparative?
v.worked: 'much *bigger than* our old one': after a comparative we use *than*.

stim.head: Letter from Ivy
stim.html:
Word box: about, are, at, both, everyone, for, than, were, who, with

Our new flat
Dear Ana,
How are you? Last month we moved to a new flat. It is (0) at the top of a tall building, and it is much bigger (18) ________ our old one. From my bedroom window I can see the river and the bridge!
When we arrived, there (19) ________ boxes everywhere, and we couldn't find our plates. Our neighbour is a friendly old man (20) ________ grows tomatoes and herbs on his balcony. He gave us a big bowl of soup on the first night.
At first I was worried (21) ________ making new friends, but (22) ________ in my new class is kind to me. My brother and I (23) ________ joining the school swimming club next week. (24) ________ my parents love the big park near our building, and we go there every evening.
Please write soon!
Love,
Ivy

v.q: Read the letter. Write ONE word from the box for gap 18.
lines: It was even bigger {0} his party last year!
v.hint: Find 'bigger'. Which box word comes after a comparative?
v.worked: 'even *bigger than* his party last year': after a comparative we use *than*.

stim.head: Letter from Phuc
stim.html:
Word box: all, am, at, by, for, on, something, than, was, which

Grandpa's birthday
Dear Finn,
Thanks (0) for your letter. Last Saturday my grandpa was seventy, so we had a family party at his house. It was even bigger (18) ________ his party last year! There (19) ________ a huge cake with seventy candles on it, and Grandpa needed help to blow them out.
My aunt cooked a special chicken soup (20) ________ Grandpa loves. Grandpa is very good (21) ________ telling funny stories, and he told us about his first job. Then I heard (22) ________ strange under the table. It was my cousin's puppy eating cake!
Next weekend I (23) ________ staying at his house for two nights. (24) ________ my cousins are staying there too, so the house will be very busy!
Write back soon!
Your friend,
Phuc

v.worked: Past + many *boxes*: there *were*.

items.en: Past simple for finished actions. Clues: *yesterday*, *last week*, *ago*. Use *there was* for one thing and *there were* for many.
items.vi: Thì quá khứ đơn cho hành động đã xong. Manh mối: *yesterday*, *last week*, *ago*. Dùng *there was* cho một vật và *there were* cho nhiều vật.

items.en: Present continuous (*am / is / are* + -ing) for now (*now*, *Look!*) and for plans with a future time (*next week*, *on Saturday*).
items.vi: Thì hiện tại tiếp diễn (*am / is / are* + -ing) cho việc đang xảy ra (*now*, *Look!*) và cho kế hoạch có thời gian tương lai (*next week*, *on Saturday*).

items.en: *-ed* adjectives say how a person feels. *-ing* adjectives describe the thing that makes you feel it. After a comparative, use *than*.
items.vi: Tính từ đuôi *-ed* nói về cảm xúc của người. Tính từ đuôi *-ing* mô tả sự vật gây ra cảm xúc đó. Sau so sánh hơn, dùng *than*.
example: The film was *boring*, so I was *bored*.

items.en: Adjective + small word: *good at*, *interested in*, *worried about*, *afraid of*, *proud of*, *kind to*, *famous for*.
items.vi: Tính từ + từ nhỏ: *good at*, *interested in*, *worried about*, *afraid of*, *proud of*, *kind to*, *famous for*.

items.en: Quantifiers: *fewer* + things you can count, *less* + things you can't count. *both* = two, *all* = three or more.
items.vi: Từ chỉ số lượng: *fewer* + thứ đếm được, *less* + thứ không đếm được. *both* = hai, *all* = ba hoặc nhiều hơn.

items.en: *who* (people), *which* (things), *where* (places). *someone / something* in positive sentences, *anyone / anything* in questions and after 'not', *nobody / nothing* = not one.
items.vi: *who* (người), *which* (vật), *where* (nơi chốn). *someone / something* trong câu khẳng định, *anyone / anything* trong câu hỏi và sau 'not', *nobody / nothing* = không ai / không gì.

check.sentence: There {were|was|is} ten candles on the cake yesterday.
My aunt {is visiting|visited|visit} us next week.
There are {fewer|less|much} cars on the road today.
This is the girl {who|which|where} helped me.

v.q:
Story: Yen's birthday picnic (sentence 1 of 5)
Last Saturday, Yen ________ her tenth birthday with a picnic in the park.
whys: 'Last Saturday' is finished time, so the base form is wrong.
'celebrating' needs 'was' before it, and the picnic is finished.
v.hint: Find the time words. Is the picnic finished?
v.worked: *Last Saturday* is finished time: Yen *celebrated* her birthday.

v.q:
Story: Zac's sore throat (sentence 1 of 5)
Last Monday, Zac ________ up with a sore throat and a runny nose.
whys: 'Last Monday' is finished time, so the base form is wrong.
'waking' needs 'was' before it, and this is a finished action.
v.hint: Find the time words. Is the action finished?
v.worked: *Last Monday* is finished time: Zac *woke* up.

v.q:
Story: Yen's birthday picnic (sentence 2 of 5)
Her little brother was very proud ________ the birthday card he made for her.
whys: 'proud at' is not English. Which small word always follows 'proud'?
'proud in' is not English. Think of 'afraid of' and 'proud ...'.
v.hint: Say the adjective and each small word quietly. Which pair do you know?
v.worked: We always say *proud of*: proud *of* the card.

v.q:
Story: Zac's sore throat (sentence 2 of 5)
He was worried ________ missing the class trip to the science museum on Friday.
whys: 'worried of' is not English. Which small word always follows 'worried'?
'worried in' is not English. Think of 'interested in' and 'worried ...'.
v.hint: Say the adjective and each small word quietly. Which pair do you know?
v.worked: We always say *worried about*: worried *about* missing the trip.

v.q:
Story: Yen's birthday picnic (sentence 3 of 5)
There were ________ sandwiches than cakes, so the sandwiches finished first.
whys: 'less' is for things we can't count, like water. We can count sandwiches.
'much' is for things we can't count, like rice. We can count sandwiches.
v.hint: Look at the noun after the gap. Can you count it?
v.worked: *sandwiches* can be counted, so we use *fewer*: fewer sandwiches, so they finished first.

v.q:
Story: Zac's sore throat (sentence 3 of 5)
The doctor said he should eat ________ sugar and drink more warm water.
whys: 'fewer' is for things we can count. We can't count sugar.
'many' is for things we can count, like sweets, not sugar.
v.hint: Look at the noun after the gap. Can you count it?
v.worked: *sugar* can't be counted, so we use *less*: less sugar, more water.

v.q:
Story: Yen's birthday picnic (sentence 4 of 5)
After lunch, they had a walk by the lake ________ the ducks and swans live.
whys: 'which' is for things, but here the lake is the place the ducks live.
'who' is for people, but a lake is not a person.
v.hint: Look at the word before the gap. Is it a person, a thing or a place?
v.worked: The lake is the place the ducks live: the lake *where* the ducks live.

v.q:
Story: Zac's sore throat (sentence 4 of 5)

whys: 'who' is for people, but a drink is a thing.
'where' is for places, but a drink is a thing.
v.hint: Look at the words before the gap. Is it a person, a thing or a place?
v.worked: A drink is a thing, so we use *which*: a hot drink *which* had honey in it.

v.q:
Story: Yen's birthday picnic (sentence 5 of 5)
At the end, there wasn't ________ left in the picnic basket, not even one biscuit.
whys: After 'not' we don't use 'something'.
'wasn't nothing' has two 'not' words. In English we use only one.
v.hint: Find 'wasn't'. Which word goes after 'not'?
v.worked: After *wasn't* we use *anything*: there wasn't anything left.

v.q:
Story: Zac's sore throat (sentence 5 of 5)
By Friday he felt better, so ________ stopped him from going on the trip.
whys: 'anything' is for questions and sentences with 'not'.
'so' tells us he could go. If something stopped him, he couldn't go.
v.hint: Read the start: he felt better. Could he go on the trip?
v.worked: He felt better, *so* he could go: *nothing* stopped him.
